title: Volunteer Orientation: Making Language Accessible
description: An introduction for new and prospective volunteers: how MSC makes language education more accessible, and how you can help. No experience needed.

title: Self-Advocacy Basics: Asking for What Helps
description: Practical, low-pressure ways to ask for what helps you understand and take part: more time, another way to respond, or a clearer explanation. It's about access and being understood.

title: Language Access 101: An Introduction for Families
description: A plain-language introduction to what language access means, and simple ways to make everyday language more flexible and inclusive. For families, students, and anyone curious. Educational, not clinical.

title: Everyday Conversational Spanish for Beginners
description: A relaxed, hands-on session on the practical, everyday Spanish people actually use: greetings, small talk, and getting around. Great for beginners. No pressure, just practice.

title: Plain-Language Writing Workshop
description: How to rewrite flyers, forms, and announcements so every family can understand them, with live before-and-after rewrites from the audience.

title: Bilingual Parenting & School Language
description: Practical strategies for parents navigating parent-teacher conferences, school forms, and everyday appointments across two languages.

title: Community Language Access 101
description: What language access is, why it matters in schools and the community, and how organizations can start improving it today.

title: Supporting Your Neurodivergent Learner at Home
description: A welcoming, practical session for families of neurodivergent learners. We share flexible, everyday ways to support language and learning at home, while respecting each child's own language style. Educational only; not clinical advice. Captions provided.

title: Language Looks Different for Everyone: A Family Introduction
description: A plain-language introduction, for families, to how people process and use language differently. The focus is understanding and respect, not changing how anyone uses language. Language preferences and support needs differ from person to person. With live Q&A and Spanish interpretation.

title: Everyday Self-Advocacy: Helping Kids Ask for What Helps
description: Practical, low-pressure ways families can support a child's self-advocacy: asking for more time, another way to respond, or a clearer explanation. It's about access and being understood, not about fitting in. Bring your questions; we practice together. Captions provided.

title: Neurodivergent & Bilingual: Two Languages as a Strength
description: Raising a bilingual, neurodivergent child is not something to worry about. More than one language is an asset. This affirming session addresses common questions and shares welcoming ways to support language across both languages at home. Educational, not clinical. Captions and Spanish interpretation provided.

title: Comunicación flexible para familias (en español)
description: Una sesión práctica en español para familias: formas flexibles y respetuosas de apoyar la comunicación en casa, reconociendo que cada persona se comunica de manera diferente. Es educativa y no reemplaza la orientación de un profesional. Con subtítulos.
